Theme

Body, health & movement

mask noun

a face mask

also face mask, surgical mask, dust mask

* our formation

* (our own formation) ōris tegimentum

phrase: tegimentum, tegimentī n., with the genitive of ōs

a covering for the mouth

Our description; no reference work has a word for a face mask. The thing is ancient: workers polishing minium tied loose bladders over their faces so as not to breathe the dust, faciem laxīs vēsīcīs inligant (Plin. NH 33.122, in Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • persōna, persōnae f. — a mask

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Phaedr. 1.7.1 (Lewis & Short); Levi–Bini p. 40

    Classically the actor’s mask over the whole head; Levi–Bini give it for any mask. For a face mask it suggests a disguise.

Examples

  • Ōris tegimentum indue; in medicīnam intrāmus.

    Put your mask on; we’re going into the doctor’s.composed

See also doctor, doctor’s surgery.

SourcesLewis & Short: tegimentum · Lewis & Short: os · Lewis & Short: persona · Lewis & Short: vesica

Enrico Levi and Arturo Bini, Il latino come lingua viva (1937), p. 40 (maschera).

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
